claim: 'we estimate that India had around 77 lakh (7.7 million) gig workers in 2020-21, forming 2.6% of the non-agricultural workforce and 1.5% of the total livelihood'
population: 'Workers with gig worker-like characteristics', platform + non-platform, India (NITI model on PLFS 2019-20 base of 68 lakh)
source_title: NITI Aayog, India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy (Jun 2022), section 2.5
notes: Read in the primary PDF. NITI itself says it is an estimate of 'workers with gig worker-like characteristics' rather than of gig workers. Includes non-platform task work.

claim: Table 14 'Projection for Gig Work using Employment Growth': gig workers 1.27 crore (2024-25 projected), 1.43 crore (2025-26 projected), 2.35 crore (2029-30 projected) = 6.68% of non-agri and 4.13% of total employment in 2029-30
population: Gig workers, platform + non-platform, India (NITI projection)
source_title: NITI Aayog, India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy (Jun 2022), Table 14
notes: A 2022 PROJECTION, not a count. Press in 2026 quotes '14.3 million gig workers in 2025-26' as if measured; it is this projection. Projection base is NITI's 54.54 crore employment (SIZE-23), not PLFS.

claim: 'about 26.6 lakh gig workers were involved in retail trade and sales, and about 1.3 million were in the transportation sector. About 6.2 lakhs were in the manufacturing and another 6.3 lakhs in the finance and insurance activities'
population: Gig workers (NITI estimate), India, by industry
source_title: NITI Aayog, India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy (Jun 2022), section 2.3
notes: About half of NITI's gig workers are in retail and transport; the rest are task workers across industries, many of them not on apps.

claim: Economic Survey 2025-26 (citing the Indian Staffing Federation): gig workforce about 1.2 crore in FY25, up from 77 lakh in FY21
population: Gig workers as counted by the Indian Staffing Federation, incl. staffing-type gigs (e-commerce 37 lakh, logistics 15 lakh, BFSI 10 lakh, manufacturing 10 lakh)
source_title: Economic Survey 2025-26, ch.12
notes: Carried from research/tri_facts.csv TF-04 (confirmed verbatim there). An industry-body estimate; method not published. Within 6% of NITI's 1.27 crore projection for the same year.

claim: 'As of date, around 11.5 lakh platform workers have registered on the portal' (e-Shram); e-Shram total 31.89 crore registrations; eligibility: unorganised worker aged 16+ who is 'not ... an income tax-payer' or EPFO/ESIC member
population: Platform workers self- or aggregator-registered on e-Shram, cumulative
source_title: PIB, '5 Years of e-Shram Portal' (25 Aug 2026)
notes: Read in the primary PDF. The only government COUNT, and under 1/10 of the estimates (GIG-02, GIG-04). Income-tax payers are excluded, so e-Shram under-counts exactly the higher earners this section is about. Supersedes the '3.37 lakh' in research/regulation_rails.csv REG-060.

claim: PIB backgrounder: 'aggregators are now required to contribute 1-2% of their annual turnover (capped at 5% of payments made or payable to gig/platform workers) to a Social Security Fund'; each worker gets an Aadhaar-linked e-Shram ID so benefits are portable across platforms
population: Aggregators (ride-sharing, delivery, logistics, e-marketplace etc.) and their gig/platform workers
source_title: PIB Backgrounder 'Labour Reforms: Formalising and Safeguarding India's Gig & Platform Workforce' (9 Dec 2025)
notes: Read via the PIB page. The fund pays for government welfare schemes (accident, health, maternity, pension). It holds no money in the worker's name and has no savings or credit feature, so it is an insurance floor, not a pipe.

claim: Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 notified 8 May 2026; aggregators to register and upload all engaged gig/platform workers within 45 days (by 21 Jun 2026) and new workers in real time
population: Aggregators and gig/platform workers, India
source_title: Outlook Business and others (search summaries); research/regulation_rails.csv REG-063
notes: Consistent across several secondary sources; the gazette was not opened.

claim: Urban Company: 'The contribution payable by platforms towards gig workers' social security has not yet been specified' (Jan 2026). Our Oct 2026 searches found no notification of the rate
population: Aggregator contribution rate under the Code on Social Security
source_title: Urban Company Q3 FY26 shareholders' letter (23 Jan 2026), NSE filing
notes: UC statement is primary. 'No notification found by Oct 2026' is absence of evidence (searched news and PIB), not proof.

claim: Swiggy average monthly transacting delivery partners Q1 FY27 = 648,000 (Q1-Q4 FY26: 606k / 691k / 687k / 612k)
population: Unique delivery partners delivering >= 1 order in a month, averaged over the quarter (Swiggy definition)
source_title: Swiggy Q1 FY27 shareholder letter
notes: Carried from research/tri_facts.csv TF-12 (PDF read there). 'At least one order a month' includes occasional riders. Riders multi-app, so platform counts in GIG-09 to GIG-15 cannot be added.

claim: Zomato food delivery average monthly active delivery partners 4.73 lakh (FY25); Blinkit 4.09 lakh (Q4 FY26); Zepto 2.87 lakh average active (DRHP)
population: Average monthly active delivery partners on each platform (definitions differ)
source_title: Eternal FY25 annual report and KPI sheet via search snippets; Zepto DRHP via aggregator
notes: Carried from research/market_benchmarks.csv SEG-06, SEG-07, SEG-08 (not opened there). Not additive.

claim: Rapido: '2 Mn transacting bike taxi partners every month' and 20 Mn transacting users; FY25 subscription income from captains and users Rs 275 cr (about 14x)
unit: lakh transacting bike-taxi partners a month (claim)
population: Rapido bike-taxi partners transacting in a month

notes: Search summaries; pages not opened. Bike-taxi partners are mostly part-time and low-earning; the count matters for reach, not for the > Rs 30k slice.

claim: Moove (Uber's vehicle-finance partner) launched in India targeting 'India's 600,000+ Uber drivers'; finances new vehicles 'using a percentage of their weekly revenue'; 5,000 vehicles in year 1, 30,000 in 5 years
population: Uber drivers in India (all vehicle types, as stated at launch)
source_title: Outlook Business, 'Uber's vehicle partner Moove launches operations in India' (26 Jul 2022)
notes: Old (2022). Also research/market_benchmarks.csv SEG-09: Uber '1.5M+ driver partners' (2025 claim, unverified). No monthly-active driver count for Uber, Ola or Rapido cars was found.

claim: Porter works with 'over 3 Lakh driver partners'
population: Porter driver partners (goods vehicles), registered, India
source_title: Inc42 / Entrackr on Porter FY25 (search summary)
notes: Search summary, not opened. Porter's FY25 revenue was Rs 4,306 cr. No earnings figure for Porter drivers was found.

claim: Urban Company monthly active service partners: 59,475 in Q3 FY26 (whole company) and 46,625 in India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp; FY25 averages 47,833 and 45,619
population: UC service professionals who delivered >= 1 service in the month, averaged over the quarter; India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp
source_title: Urban Company Q3 FY26 shareholders' letter (23 Jan 2026), NSE filing
notes: Read in the primary PDF (Operating Metrics tables). Excludes extra staff hired by partners.

claim: UC Partner Earnings Index 9M FY26, all partners: average monthly gross earnings Rs 55,244; UC commissions & fees 28.3%; indirect tax (589); travel (2,662); product + additional personnel costs (8,061); 'Net earnings in hand per partner per month' Rs 28,322; 91 hours a month
population: All active UC service partners, India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp
source_title: Urban Company Q3 FY26 shareholders' letter (23 Jan 2026), NSE filing, Partner Earnings Index
notes: Company-published. Net = after commission, travel and product costs. The best primary GROSS-to-NET example in India: net is 51% of gross.

claim: UC partners delivering > 30 orders a month = 65% of monthly active partners: average gross Rs 66,383, net Rs 35,637, 114 hours a month
population: UC partners delivering > 30 orders a month (65% of monthly active), India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp
source_title: Urban Company Q3 FY26 shareholders' letter (23 Jan 2026), NSE filing, Partner Earnings Index
notes: An AVERAGE for the group; not every member nets > Rs 30k.

claim: UC top partners by orders: top 20% net Rs 42,418 (gross 82,026); top 10% net Rs 47,471; top 5% net Rs 51,673
population: Top 20% / 10% / 5% of UC monthly active partners ranked by orders
source_title: Urban Company Q3 FY26 shareholders' letter (23 Jan 2026), NSE filing, Partner Earnings Index
notes: Ranked by ORDERS, not by earnings, so percentile bands are approximate earnings bands.

claim: DERIVED: UC partners who net more than Rs 30k a month: at least ~9,300 (top 20% x 46,625) and plausibly up to ~30,300 (65% doing > 30 orders x 46,625). The 80th-90th percentile band averages (0.20 x 42,418 - 0.10 x 47,471) / 0.10 = Rs 37,365 net
population: UC monthly active partners, India Consumer Services ex-InstaHelp
as_of: 9M FY26 earnings x Q3 FY26 count
source_title: Derived from GIG-14, GIG-16, GIG-17
notes: Mixes a 9-month earnings period with a Q3 partner count from the same company and segment. The lower bound assumes everyone in the top 20% nets > Rs 30k, which the Rs 37,365 band average supports.

claim: IDinsight: consistent full-time delivery riders: gross Rs 27,814 a month; expenses ~32% (fuel/charging 23%, repairs 5%); net Rs 18,761; 62.2 hours a week. EV riders gross 32,717 / net 24,370; motorbike riders gross 27,286 / net 18,167. 'some drivers earn as high as Rs. 80,000 per month which is over 3 times higher than the median'
population: Consistent full-time two-wheeler delivery riders on one Indian platform (population > 5 lakh), 2024; admin earnings + survey costs
source_title: IDinsight, DERII India descriptive study report (Feb 2025), section 5.5.2
notes: Read in the primary PDF. Even EV riders' NET (24,370) is below Rs 30k. 77% of the full sample work <= 8 hours a day (research/market_benchmarks.csv INC-01). The report cites Morgan Stanley (2024): delivery net income Rs 18,500-21,500.

claim: Dvara diaries: participants earned Rs 35,075 a month gross from platforms on average, but fuel, commission and other work costs cut NET platform income to Rs 16,604
population: 22 platform workers (delivery, auto, cab, home services), Bengaluru financial diaries
source_title: Dvara Research, The financial lives of platform workers: a diaries study in Bengaluru (Dec 2023)
notes: Carried from research/segments.csv SG-20. Tiny sample, but shows a > Rs 30k GROSS worker netting under Rs 17k.

claim: PAIGAM/IFAT survey: '43 percent cab drivers ... earn below Rs 500 per day (after deducting cost of fuel, food, etc.)'; '34.4 percent of the delivery persons earn less than Rs 10,000 a month after deducting all their monthly expenses'; 72% of drivers could not meet monthly expenses
unit: % of cab drivers below Rs 500 a day net
population: 5,308 app-based cab drivers and 5,028 delivery persons, 8 cities
source_title: The Quint on PAIGAM and IFAT survey (11 Mar 2024)
notes: Article read; survey by worker-advocacy groups (method not published in the article). Rs 500 a day x 30 days = Rs 15,000 a month net.

claim: 'About 40 per cent of gig workers report earnings below Rs 15,000 per month' (Economic Survey 2025-26 para 12.38, citing the Indian Staffing Federation)
unit: % of gig workers below Rs 15,000 a month
population: Gig workers as counted by the Indian Staffing Federation (incl. staffing-type gigs)
source_title: Economic Survey 2025-26, ch.12
notes: Carried from research/segments.csv SG-03 / tri_facts.csv TF-01. Gross or net not stated, so never compare with GIG-15 to GIG-21.

claim: No platform other than Urban Company publishes an earnings DISTRIBUTION for its partners; no national source counts gig workers earning > Rs 30k a month, gross or net
population: Gig/platform workers, India
source_title: Our search: Swiggy and Eternal shareholder letters, Uber, Ola, Rapido, Porter disclosures, Fairwork India 2024, PAIGAM/IFAT, IDinsight, Economic Survey
notes: Absence of evidence after the searches listed, not proof. Fairwork India 2024 rates platforms but publishes no rupee earnings; it gave Ola, Porter and Uber 0/10.

claim: BOUNDED ESTIMATE: gig workers NETTING > Rs 30k a month = tens of thousands evidenced (UC ~9,300-30,300, GIG-18) and, by our judgement, at most low lakhs once owner-drivers of cabs and goods vehicles are added (no source for their net income)
population: Gig/platform workers, India
source_title: Derived from GIG-18, GIG-19, GIG-21, GIG-23
notes: The upper end is judgement, not arithmetic. Full-time riders average Rs 18.8k net (EV 24.4k), and 43% of cab drivers net under Rs 15k, so > Rs 30k net is a minority everywhere except skilled home services.

claim: BOUNDED ESTIMATE: gig workers GROSSING > Rs 30k a month: at most ~33 lakh = 1.43 crore (GIG-02, 2025-26 projection) x ~23% full-time (IDinsight: 77% of riders work <= 8 hours a day)
population: Gig workers, India (NITI projection) x full-time share from one delivery platform
source_title: Derived from GIG-02 and IDinsight (research/market_benchmarks.csv INC-01)
notes: Crude: it applies a full-time share measured on one delivery platform to NITI's whole gig estimate, and not every full-timer grosses Rs 30k (full-time riders average Rs 27.8k gross). Use only as a ceiling, never as a count.

claim: IDinsight: having a bank account is an entry requirement for platform work and is 'used by [platform] to transfer earnings'; all respondents had one (99% had one before joining)
population: Delivery riders on one Indian platform, 2024 survey
source_title: IDinsight, DERII India descriptive study report (Feb 2025)
notes: Platform pay lands in the WORKER's own bank account, unlike a shop QR where the payments app settles to the merchant's account it chose.

claim: Uber India drivers 'can cash their earnings any day of the week, once they had earned a minimum amount of Rs 200', 'instead of waiting for their weekly cashouts'
value: weekly default; any day from Rs 200
population: Uber driver-partners in India (Moto, Auto, cars)
source_title: The News Minute, 'Uber allows drivers to cash out earnings any day of the week' (26 Nov 2020)
notes: Old (2020) but still the documented cadence. For Uber Auto it no longer applies (GIG-28).

claim: Uber Auto (from Feb 2025): drivers pay 'a fee between ... 20-40 Indian rupees per day'; 'Riders will need to pay the driver directly in cash or digitally via ... UPI'. 'Rapido and Namma Yatri don't charge a commission; their model is more subscription-based'
population: Uber auto-rickshaw drivers, all India
source_title: TechCrunch, 'Uber ditches commissions in favor of fees for auto-rickshaw drivers in India' (19 Feb 2025)
notes: Article read. When the passenger pays the driver directly, the platform never holds the money, so it cannot deduct a loan EMI. These drivers now get paid on their own UPI QR, like a shop.

claim: Ola extended zero-commission to cabs (Jun 2025): 30-day pass Rs 2,010 or Rs 67 a day. Rapido: access fee 'Rs 9-29 per day' plus Rs 500 subscription if monthly earnings exceed Rs 10,000 (since 2024). Namma Yatri: Rs 3.5 a trip or Rs 25 a day
population: Ola cab drivers; Rapido captains; Namma Yatri drivers
source_title: Medianama, 'Ola expands zero-commission model to cab drivers' (19 Jun 2025)
notes: Article read. It does not say how Ola cab passengers pay, so do not assume direct UPI for Ola cabs.

claim: Swiggy 'Early Cashout': food delivery partners can withdraw earnings any time from the Partner app and receive them 'within an hour', instead of waiting for weekly payouts
population: Swiggy Food Marketplace delivery partners
source_title: Restaurant India, 'Swiggy introduces Early Cashout for food delivery partners' (18 Sep 2026)
notes: Article read. Default cycle remains weekly. Fees and limits not stated.

claim: Porter: partner payment is credited to a wallet in the driver app at the end of each trip and can be moved to the bank any time; previously a weekly cycle that could take up to 11 days
population: Porter driver partners
source_title: Cashfree case study on Porter (vendor marketing)
notes: Search summary of a payments vendor's case study; not opened; date unknown.

claim: Mutual fund subscriptions must come from the investor's own bank account (SEBI Master Circular for MFs, 20 Mar 2026, cl.17.4); SEBI's May 2026 draft would allow third-party payment only by listed/EPFO-registered EMPLOYERS
population: Mutual fund investors, India
source_title: research/regulation_rails.csv REG-066
notes: Carried. A platform cannot pay into a worker's fund directly: money must land in the worker's bank first, then the worker's own UPI AutoPay pulls it. That is exactly the 'own-name' pipe shape.

claim: Swiggy and Zerodha Fund House: delivery partners can invest in mutual funds from Rs 100 directly in the Swiggy Rider app, zero lock-in, withdraw any time; managed via Zerodha Fund House's WhatsApp channel
population: Swiggy delivery partners
source_title: BusinessToday (25 Jun 2026); HR Katha (26 Jun 2026)
notes: Launched Jun 2026. Uptake not disclosed. Whether it auto-saves from payouts is not stated. Supersedes research/tri_behaviour.csv TB-45 ('no launch date').

claim: Swiggy facilitated Rs 102 crore of loans to delivery partners in the 12 months to Dec 2023 and receives over 1.5 lakh loan applications a month
population: Swiggy delivery partners
source_title: Business Standard (12 Dec 2023)
notes: Carried from research/segments.csv SG-17. Rs 102 cr / 12 = ~Rs 8.5 cr a month.

claim: Urban Company facilitated 'INR 37.2 crores worth of loans, including personal loans and service kit loans' via third-party NBFCs (FY24); NPS with HDFC Pension; group life cover Rs 10 lakh and disability Rs 6 lakh for active partners
population: Urban Company service professionals
source_title: Urban Company IR, service professional enablement; UC Q3 FY26 letter
notes: Loans carried from research/segments.csv SG-16; insurance and NPS from the UC earnings-index page read today.

claim: Zomato and Blinkit spent about Rs 100 cr a year on delivery-partner insurance premiums (accident up to Rs 10 lakh, medical Rs 1 lakh), free to the rider
population: Zomato + Blinkit delivery partners
source_title: Inc42 (search summary)
notes: Carried from research/tri_costs.csv TC-26. Platforms already give the obvious insurance free; an outside app can only top up.

claim: NeoGrowth-Zomato: 'EXCLUSIVE LOANS FOR YOUR RESTAURANT', Rs 2-75 lakh at 21.5% APR; 'Zomato will make your payouts in an E-collect account managed by NeoGrowth; NeoGrowth will deduct a pre-agreed fixed amount ... and release the balance ... within 1 working day'
population: Zomato RESTAURANT partners (not delivery partners)
source_title: NeoGrowth-Zomato partner page
notes: Page read. CORRECTS research/lend_self.csv LS-04 and tables/deck_facts.csv 'payout_deduction', which say this applies to delivery partners. It is the restaurant (merchant) version of EMI-from-settlement.

claim: Uber (2016, Mumbai): leased cars' 'low weekly rental ... is deducted from the Uber payment itself'; vehicle loans via Toyota FS, Tata Motor Finance, AU, Shriram, Mahindra Finance, EMIs over 4-5 years. Moove (2022): repayment as a % of weekly Uber revenue (GIG-12)
population: Uber driver-partners using partner leasing (2016) or Moove financing (2022)
source_title: Uber India blog 'Want to be an Uber Mumbai partner' (8 Sep 2016); Outlook Business (2022)
notes: Pages read. Shows deduction from ride-hailing payouts HAS existed for vehicle finance; we found no current (2025-26) public statement that it still runs.

claim: Founder's past lending data: the platform channel produced cheaper borrowers who repaid better; the platform charged Rs 200 per loan for its data and deducted repayments from payouts at source. The employer channel failed (small market; first loan not profitable from day one)
population: Founder's past lending business, platform-sourced loans
source_title: Founder's past lending data (tables/inputs_founder_*.csv: platform fee, platform vs ads, employer channel rows)
notes: Founder's own data; 'cheaper and repaid better' has no numbers attached. First loans were Rs 10-25k for 3 months with 6-7% never repaid (same file).

claim: No current public evidence that a delivery or ride-hailing platform deducts a third-party lender's EMI from gig workers' payouts
population: Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit, Zepto, Uber, Ola, Rapido, Porter
source_title: Our search ('EMI deducted from weekly payout' + platform names; lender pages; platform IR)
notes: Absence of evidence, not proof. Known cases are the founder's past deal (GIG-39), Uber leasing 2016 and Moove 2022 (GIG-38), and restaurant loans (GIG-37). Lenders today underwrite on payout credits in the BANK statement and collect by mandate.

claim: Bachatt homepage: 'Bachatt is a savings app for every Indian - salaried professionals, shop owners, jewellers, dealers, manufacturers, factory owners and the people who work with them'; no mention of gig, delivery or driver partners
population: Bachatt target customers (company copy)
source_title: bachatt.app homepage
notes: Read today. Seed-stage press (2025) mentioned gig workers; current copy does not. Homepage still shows '10 Lakh+' users and '50+ Cr' invested.

claim: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act 2025: welfare fee notified at 1% of payout per transaction, capped at Rs 0.50-1.50 per transaction (rules notified 19 Nov 2025); the High Court directed Swiggy, Zomato, Blinkit and Zepto to deposit the fee for a quarter (Jul 2026)
population: Platforms operating in Karnataka
source_title: research/regulation_rails.csv REG-064; Business Standard explainer (8 Jul 2026, search summary)
notes: Fee detail carried; court order from a search summary (page returned 403). A per-transaction fee tagged to each payout shows payouts CAN be tapped by law; the money goes to a state board, not to the worker.

claim: Telangana passed its Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) Act on 1 Apr 2026 with a 1-2% levy on transactions for a welfare fund; fifth state after Rajasthan (2023), Karnataka (2025), Jharkhand (2025), Bihar (2025). 'Except for Jharkhand, other states face implementation challenges'; Rajasthan and Bihar progress 'stalled'
population: Platforms operating in Telangana; state gig laws
source_title: VisionIAS summary of The Indian Express (1 Apr 2026)
notes: Secondary summary read. Rajasthan's 2023 Act has no rules framed (research/regulation_rails.csv REG-065). None of these laws creates a savings account in the worker's name.

claim: IDinsight: 'Approximately 39% of respondents are able to save'; of savers 77% save in a bank, 13% in cash, 14% send money to family. 39% faced an emergency since joining, averaging Rs 61,456; of those, 47% borrowed from a moneylender, 38% from friends/family, 10% from a bank; 'Only 8% ... were able to use their current savings'
population: Delivery riders on one Indian platform, 2024 survey
source_title: IDinsight, DERII India descriptive study report (Feb 2025), section 5.7
notes: Read in the primary PDF. The demand is for a cushion big enough for a Rs 61k shock; today it comes from moneylenders.

claim: Dvara diaries: NONE of 22 participants saved in FD, RD, post office, pension or mutual funds; chit funds were the most used (9 of 22); some started FDs/RDs and stopped within a couple of months
population: 22 platform workers (delivery, auto, cab, home services), Bengaluru
source_title: Dvara Research, The financial lives of platform workers: a diaries study in Bengaluru (Dec 2023)
notes: Carried from research/segments.csv SG-19. Small sample.

claim: Borzo survey: 77% of gig/delivery workers hold no mutual funds; 65% have no life insurance
population: Gig/delivery workers, 40 cities (Borzo, a delivery company)
source_title: East Asia Forum citing Borzo (9 Apr 2026)
notes: Carried from research/xs_other.csv XO-32; method unknown, interested party.

claim: No data found on gig workers using Janta / pigmy / daily-deposit agents, or on their gold savings
population: Gig/platform workers, India
source_title: Our search (IDinsight, Dvara, Fairwork, PAIGAM, news)
